critical_code_review_comments: CarePlanReviewer.jsx: the pre-fix code declared PROGRESS_STAGES + progressStage state + useEffect(loading) BEFORE `const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)`. React const declarations are block-scoped and in TDZ until the useState line is reached, so the first render (before any state has settled) throws immediately. Rule of thumb: keep all useState() declarations at the top of the component, then useEffect() below — or use useLayoutEffect. Would benefit from `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` + eslint `no-use-before-define` set to error for lets/consts inside components.

cpr_mitigate is now a pass-through per backend agent handoff, and the FE guard `(result?.safety_notice || fileResult?.safety_notice)` correctly hides the banner when both are null. Verified live: banner not rendered on a 9-finding result. Good.

CarePlanStore.jsx:144 uses window.confirm for the hard-delete confirmation. Works functionally but is jarring (native OS dialog inside a paid app UX). Consider a themed AlertDialog for the 'Delete forever' step — the softDelete path uses window.confirm too, so the inconsistency isn't specific to this feature.

CarePlanReviewer.jsx:514-516 renders `Source: {f.citation_source}` unconditionally when citation_source is truthy — good defensive fallback. But when the backend sets citation_source='Verification required' for every freeform finding, the UX effectively shows 9 identical grey 'Verification required' lines under otherwise-varied findings, which reduces the perceived value of the citation flow. Consider only rendering the Source: line when citation_source is a real registry citation and hiding it (or showing an explicit 'no citation available' subtle badge) otherwise.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the reviewer-page crash: CarePlanReviewer.jsx placed the B2 progress state (`const [progressStage,...]`) AND its driving useEffect above the `const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)` declaration. The effect closed over `loading`, but at the moment the effect's dependency array `[loading]` was evaluated on initial mount, `loading` was still in JavaScript's temporal dead zone (block-scoped const not yet initialized). Result: ReferenceError at the very first render — before any state settled — surfaced by React's error boundary as a 500-styled 'Something on our side broke.' page. Fix: reorder — declare all useState() rows first, then place useEffect(fn, [loading]) after them so `loading` is initialized when the effect body / deps evaluate. Fix applied in-place. All downstream mission checks (banner retirement, Source: line, regression, C3 dialog) confirmed after the reorder.
